Democrats Win Alaska
Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola
won the last undecided Senate seat
last night, AP projects, defeating two-term incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) with 50.1% of the vote as of this writing. The victory brings Democrats to a 56-44 Senate majority, their largest since the 2008 election.
Peltola's campaign was accused last month of recruiting two candidates, including one who shares the incumbent's name, to confuse voters and siphon votes (
read previous write-up
). The allegations prompted an unsuccessful Justice Department lawsuit to block certification of the results if Peltola narrowly won. Ultimately, the latest tally, with a gap of over 12,000 votes as of this writing shows that combining Sen. Sullivan's votes with the two minor candidates would not have been enough to overcome Peltola's lead. She is the first Democrat Alaska has sent to the Senate in nearly two decades.
Separately, seven House races
remain uncalled
(w/map), though Democrats have already secured at least a 257-seat majority. House Democrats are expected to nominate Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-08) to serve as House speaker today.

Light-Days Ahead
NASA’s Voyager 1 space probe is on track to
reach one light-day
from Earth this morning at 5:16 am ET. By traveling over 16 billion miles, the spacecraft is due to become the first human-made object to cross the interstellar milestone. See a graphic depicting how far other objects have traveled from Earth
here
Voyager 1 launched in September 1977 with the goal of collecting data and
images of the solar system
. It became the farthest human-made object from Earth in 1998 when it traveled roughly 6.5 billion miles to surpass the mark set by NASA’s Pioneer 10 space probe. NASA anticipates Voyager 1 will continue measuring magnetic fields and plasma waves before losing power for contact around 2036.
If it encounters alien life, Voyager 1 is equipped with messages from Earth on the Golden Record. The disk contains songs, images, sounds from nature, greetings in 55 languages, and illustrated instructions to play it. Listen to its contents
here

Crimea Bridge Strike
Ukraine
struck the Crimea Bridge
yesterday, destroying an estimated 900 feet of road surface, halting road traffic, and collapsing one of its two arches into the water. Watch alleged footage of the operation
here
(via YouTube).
Ukraine characterized the strike as the final stage of a seven-part assault on the bridge connecting Crimea to Russia's southwestern region of Krasnodar Krai. The weekslong operation included drone strikes on Russian air defense and radar systems. The attack fell short of a blockade; rail traffic resumed yesterday on the uncollapsed portion of the bridge. There is also a land corridor to Crimea through the occupied Ukrainian regions of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson, though that passageway is often subject to drone strikes. See before-and-after images of the bridge
here
(scroll and slide).
The attack also carries symbolic value: Russia annexed Crimea in March 2014, with construction of the bridge beginning in 2016. Russian President Vladimir Putin inaugurated the Crimea Bridge in May 2018 (
